# An Agent-Based Approach to Intelligent Car Parking Management and Data Analytics for Sustainability

MSc Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Keele University · Module CSC-44120 · Muhammad Faryad · Supervisor: Dr Thomas Neligwa

A working multi-agent parking simulation with two allocation strategies, replicated paired experiments, analytics, and a local dashboard.
**All data are synthetic** (generated by `src/parking_mas/datagen.py`); nothing was collected from real car parks, drivers or sensors.

## 1. Features
Event-driven simulation · Vehicle / Parking-space / Car-park / Management agents with explicit messages · baseline and coordinated strategies · 7 predefined scenarios · reproducible seeds · structured logs · metrics with documented definitions · paired statistics · 7 figures · Streamlit dashboard (live play/pause/resume/step/reset) · 62 automated tests · Windows `.bat` launchers.

## 2. Architecture, agents, strategies, lifecycle
See `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/algorithms.md`. Summary: vehicles request → manager queries car parks → strategy ranks candidates → manager offers in order → vehicle accepts (walk limit) or declines → allocate / wait / fail; departures release the exact space and retry the waiting queue. Coordination is centralised (not decentralised negotiation).
Baseline = first eligible free space in fixed car-park order. Coordinated = lowest weighted cost of drive distance, walk distance, car-park congestion, with EV/accessible bay credits.

## 3. Metrics and synthetic data
`docs/metrics.md` (numerator, denominator, unit, window; emission proxy assumptions) and `docs/data_dictionary.md`. The CO2e figure is an **assumption-based simulation proxy**, not measured impact.

## 4. Install, run, test (Windows)
Needs Python 3.10+. Double-click in this order:
`INSTALL.bat` → `CHECK_ENVIRONMENT.bat` → `RUN_TESTS.bat` → `RUN.bat` (http://localhost:8501).
`RUN_DEMO.bat` loads `configs/demo_config.json` (seed 2026). `REPRODUCE_RESULTS.bat` reruns the experiments (asks before overwriting).
Command line (after install, from the project folder):
```
.venv\Scripts\python -m parking_mas.cli experiment --mode research --seed 2026 --overwrite
.venv\Scripts\python -m parking_mas.cli analyse results\research
.venv\Scripts\python -m parking_mas.cli run --scenario high_demand --strategy baseline
.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest -q
```
(Set `PYTHONPATH=src` if you are not using the .bat files.)

## 5. Results and chart locations
`results/research/` (7 scenarios × 30 replications × 2 strategies, seed 2026) and `results/demo/` (2 × 5). Each holds `runs.csv`, `occupancy_timeseries.csv`, `decision_log_replication0.csv`, `summary_by_scenario.csv`, `comparison_paired.csv`, `tables.md`, `metadata.json`, `figures/*.png`.
These files were generated by the code in this repository; `metadata.json` records versions and mode.

What the included research run shows (model-specific, synthetic; read `tables.md` for intervals):
* Success rate and waiting time: no practically meaningful difference between strategies in most scenarios (differences ≤ ~0.3 percentage points; Holm-adjusted p mostly > 0.05 in high_demand, small_capacity).
* Coordinated reduces mean walking distance (≈ 6–226 m depending on scenario) and raises the share of EVs in EV bays.
* Coordinated **increases** mean drive distance and therefore the CO2e proxy (≈ +0.8 to +7.3 kg per run) because the default weights favour short walks over short drives. This is reported as found; it is not tuned away.
